# Feature Engineering

Features are deliberately interpretable — a Data Analyst must be able
to explain every input to a stakeholder.

```{r features}
pipe <- run_pipeline("../data/synthetic", "../data/processed")
daily <- pipe$daily
bf <- build_features(daily, "sla_attainment_pct",
                     include_operational = FALSE)
head(bf$frame[, c("date", "sla_attainment_pct", "lag_1", "lag_7",
                  "roll_mean_7", "vol_dev_28d")])
```

## Design decisions

1. **Forecaster uses lag + calendar features only.** Same-day
   operational features (staffing ratio, backlog) are explanatory,
   not forecasting inputs — using them would leak information that
   is only known after the day ends.
2. **Lags 1 / 7 / 14 / 28** capture yesterday, last week, and the
   monthly cycle. Rolling means smooth the noise.
3. **`vol_dev_28d`** (volume deviation from the 28-day rolling
   mean) is the demand-shock flag — the feature that lets the model
   react to surges instead of averaging them away.
4. **Calendar features** (day of week, weekend flag, month,
   day-of-year sin/cos) encode the weekly and annual seasonality
   found in the EDA.

## Anomaly features

```{r anomaly-feats}
hf <- anomaly_features(pipe$health)
head(hf[, c("date", "rows_received_ratio", "missing_rate_pct",
            "health_score", "is_anomaly")])
```
